017package org.apache.juneau.commons.svl.functions;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.StringUtils.*;

021import java.util.*;
022
023import org.apache.juneau.commons.svl.*;

025/**
026 * String-manipulation functions for the {@code #{...}} script catalog.
027 *
028 * <p>
029 * Each public static nested class is a {@link TypedFunction} registered under the function name
030 * shown in its {@link VarFunction#name()} method. The {@code Replaces} annotation in each
031 * nested-class Javadoc names the legacy {@code Var} class that was retired in 10.0.0 in favor of
032 * the function form.
033 */
034public final class StringFunctions {
035
036   private StringFunctions() {}
037
038   /** All function classes in this category, in registration order. */
039   @SuppressWarnings({
040      "unchecked",   // Array initializer with parameterized element type; class literals are always erased at runtime.
041      "java:S2386"   // ALL is an immutable compile-time registry; exposed as an array for the cross-package/varargs functions(...) API, so visibility cannot be reduced.
042   })
043   public static final Class<? extends VarFunction>[] ALL = new Class[] {
044      Substring.class, Upper.class, Lower.class, Trim.class, StripLeading.class,
045      StripTrailing.class, StripSlashes.class, PathToken.class, Len.class, Replace.class,
046      Contains.class, StartsWith.class, EndsWith.class, Concat.class, Repeat.class,
047      Reverse.class, Format.class, Split.class, Join.class
048   };
049
050   /**
051    * {@code #{substring(s, start)}} / {@code #{substring(s, start, end)}} — replacement for the
052    * legacy {@code $ST{...}} {@code SubstringVar}.
053    *
054    * <p>
055    * Both endpoints are clamped to {@code [0, len(s)]} so out-of-range arguments don't throw —
056    * matches the legacy {@code SubstringVar} behavior.
057    */
058   public static class Substring extends TypedFunction {
059      @Override public String name() { return "substring"; }
060      public String invoke(String s, int start) {
061         if (s == null) return "";
062         var len = s.length();
063         var a = Math.max(0, Math.min(start, len));
064         return s.substring(a);
065      }
066      public String invoke(String s, int start, int end) {
067         if (s == null) return "";
068         var len = s.length();
069         var a = Math.max(0, Math.min(start, len));
070         var b = Math.max(a, Math.min(end, len));
071         return s.substring(a, b);
072      }
073   }
074
075   /** {@code #{upper(s)}} — replacement for the legacy {@code $UC{...}}. */
076   public static class Upper extends TypedFunction {
077      @Override public String name() { return "upper"; }
078      public String invoke(String s) { return s == null ? "" : s.toUpperCase(); }
079   }
080
081   /** {@code #{lower(s)}} — replacement for the legacy {@code $LC{...}}. */
082   public static class Lower extends TypedFunction {
083      @Override public String name() { return "lower"; }
084      public String invoke(String s) { return s == null ? "" : s.toLowerCase(); }
085   }
086
087   /** {@code #{trim(s)}} — strips leading and trailing whitespace. */
088   public static class Trim extends TypedFunction {
089      @Override public String name() { return "trim"; }
090      public String invoke(String s) { return s == null ? "" : s.trim(); }
091   }
092
093   /** {@code #{stripLeading(s)}} — strips leading whitespace. */
094   public static class StripLeading extends TypedFunction {
095      @Override public String name() { return "stripLeading"; }
096      public String invoke(String s) { return s == null ? "" : s.stripLeading(); }
097   }
098
099   /** {@code #{stripTrailing(s)}} — strips trailing whitespace. */
100   public static class StripTrailing extends TypedFunction {
101      @Override public String name() { return "stripTrailing"; }
102      public String invoke(String s) { return s == null ? "" : s.stripTrailing(); }
103   }
104
105   /** {@code #{stripSlashes(s)}} — strips leading and trailing {@code /} characters. */
106   public static class StripSlashes extends TypedFunction {
107      @Override public String name() { return "stripSlashes"; }
108      public String invoke(String s) {
109         if (s == null) return "";
110         var start = 0;
111         var end = s.length();
112         while (start < end && s.charAt(start) == '/') start++;
113         while (end > start && s.charAt(end - 1) == '/') end--;
114         return s.substring(start, end);
115      }
116   }
117
118   /**
119    * {@code #{pathToken(s)}} — normalize a user-supplied path token for safe interpolation
120    * into a {@code path=} template.
121    *
122    * <p>
123    * Strips leading and trailing {@code /}, plus a trailing {@code /*} (or {@code *} that
124    * sits immediately after a {@code /}). Multi-segment paths are preserved.
125    *
126    * <h5 class='section'>Edge cases:</h5>
127    * <ul>
128    *    <li>{@code ""} → {@code ""}
129    *    <li>{@code "/"} → {@code ""}
130    *    <li>{@code "/*"} → {@code ""}
131    *    <li>{@code "jsp"} → {@code "jsp"}
132    *    <li>{@code "/jsp"} → {@code "jsp"}
133    *    <li>{@code "/jsp/"} → {@code "jsp"}
134    *    <li>{@code "/jsp/*"} → {@code "jsp"}
135    *    <li>{@code "jsp/*"} → {@code "jsp"}
136    *    <li>{@code "/api/v1/*"} → {@code "api/v1"}
137    * </ul>
138    *
139    * <p>
140    * Used in SVL-configurable mixin paths so users can supply
141    * {@code "jsp"}, {@code "/jsp"}, {@code "/jsp/"}, {@code "/jsp/*"}, or {@code "jsp/*"} and
142    * the template {@code /#{pathToken(${juneau.jsp.path:jsp})}/*} always resolves to a clean
143    * {@code /jsp/*}.
144    */
145   public static class PathToken extends TypedFunction {
146      @Override public String name() { return "pathToken"; }
147      public String invoke(String s) {
148         if (isEmpty(s)) return "";
149         var t = s;
150         // Strip a trailing /* or trailing * (when sitting right after a /).
151         if (t.endsWith("/*"))
152            t = t.substring(0, t.length() - 2);
153         else if (t.endsWith("*") && t.length() >= 2 && t.charAt(t.length() - 2) == '/')
154            t = t.substring(0, t.length() - 1);
155         // Strip leading and trailing slashes.
156         var start = 0;
157         var end = t.length();
158         while (start < end && t.charAt(start) == '/') start++;
159         while (end > start && t.charAt(end - 1) == '/') end--;
160         return t.substring(start, end);
161      }
162   }
163
164   /**
165    * {@code #{len(s)}} / {@code #{len(s, delimiter)}} — replacement for the legacy
166    * {@code $LN{...}}.
167    *
168    * <p>
169    * Single-arg form returns the character count. Two-arg form splits on the literal
170    * {@code delimiter} (after trimming leading/trailing whitespace, matching the legacy
171    * {@code LenVar} behavior) and returns the part count.
172    */
173   public static class Len extends TypedFunction {
174      @Override public String name() { return "len"; }
175      public String invoke(String s) { return s == null ? "0" : String.valueOf(s.length()); }
176      public String invoke(String s, String delimiter) {
177         if (s == null) return "0";
178         if (delimiter == null || delimiter.isEmpty()) return String.valueOf(s.length());
179         return String.valueOf(s.trim().split(java.util.regex.Pattern.quote(delimiter)).length);
180      }
181   }
182
183   /**
184    * {@code #{replace(s, target, replacement)}} — literal (non-regex) string replacement.
185    *
186    * <p>
187    * For regex replacement use {@code #{replaceRegex(s, regex, replacement)}}.
188    */
189   public static class Replace extends TypedFunction {
190      @Override public String name() { return "replace"; }
191      public String invoke(String s, String target, String replacement) {
192         if (s == null) return "";
193         return s.replace(target, replacement == null ? "" : replacement);
194      }
195   }

197   /** {@code #{contains(s, substr)}} — returns {@code "true"} or {@code "false"}. */
198   public static class Contains extends TypedFunction {
199      @Override public String name() { return "contains"; }
200      public String invoke(String s, String substr) {
201         return String.valueOf(s != null && substr != null && s.contains(substr));
202      }
203   }

205   /** {@code #{startsWith(s, prefix)}} — returns {@code "true"} or {@code "false"}. */
206   public static class StartsWith extends TypedFunction {
207      @Override public String name() { return "startsWith"; }
208      public String invoke(String s, String prefix) {
209         return String.valueOf(s != null && prefix != null && s.startsWith(prefix));
210      }
211   }
212
213   /** {@code #{endsWith(s, suffix)}} — returns {@code "true"} or {@code "false"}. */
214   public static class EndsWith extends TypedFunction {
215      @Override public String name() { return "endsWith"; }
216      public String invoke(String s, String suffix) {
217         return String.valueOf(s != null && suffix != null && s.endsWith(suffix));
218      }
219   }

221   /** {@code #{concat(s1, s2, ...)}} — variadic string concatenation. */
222   public static class Concat extends TypedFunction {
223      @Override public String name() { return "concat"; }
224      public String invoke(String[] parts) {
225         var sb = new StringBuilder();
226         for (var p : parts)
227            if (p != null) sb.append(p);
228         return sb.toString();
229      }
230   }
231
232   /** {@code #{repeat(s, n)}} — repeats {@code s} {@code n} times. */
233   public static class Repeat extends TypedFunction {
234      @Override public String name() { return "repeat"; }
235      public String invoke(String s, int n) {
236         if (s == null || n <= 0) return "";
237         return s.repeat(n);
238      }
239   }
240
241   /** {@code #{reverse(s)}} — reverses the characters of {@code s}. */
242   public static class Reverse extends TypedFunction {
243      @Override public String name() { return "reverse"; }
244      public String invoke(String s) {
245         return s == null ? "" : new StringBuilder(s).reverse().toString();
246      }
247   }

249   /**
250    * {@code #{format(pattern, args...)}} — {@link String#format Java formatter-style
251    * formatting}. Pattern uses Java {@link Formatter} syntax (e.g. {@code %s},
252    * {@code %d}, {@code %.2f}). Variadic args; coerced per Java {@code Formatter} rules at
253    * invocation.
254    *
255    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
256    * <p>
257    * {@code #{format("%s-%03d", ${prefix}, ${counter})}}
258    *
259    * <p>
260    * All args are passed as raw {@link String} values; format specifiers like {@code %d} will
261    * convert numeric strings via {@link Integer#parseInt} / {@link Long#parseLong} as needed.
262    * {@code %s} accepts any string verbatim.
263    */
264   public static class Format extends TypedFunction {
265      @Override public String name() { return "format"; }
266      public String invoke(String pattern, String[] args) {
267         if (pattern == null) return "";
268         var coerced = new Object[args.length];
269         for (var i = 0; i < args.length; i++)
270            coerced[i] = coerceArgForFormat(args[i]);
271         return String.format(pattern, coerced);
272      }
273
274      /**
275       * Best-effort numeric coercion for {@code %d}/{@code %f}-style specifiers — strings
276       * that parse as long/double are passed as the typed value, otherwise as the raw
277       * string. This keeps {@code %s} as the safe default while letting numeric specifiers
278       * work without a separate {@code numericFormat(...)} entry point.
279       */
280      @SuppressWarnings({
281         "java:S1166" // Exception swallowed — coercion is best-effort.
282      })
283      private static Object coerceArgForFormat(String s) {
284         if (s == null) return "";
285         var t = s.trim();
286         try { return Long.parseLong(t); } catch (@SuppressWarnings("unused") NumberFormatException e) { /* fall through */ }
287         try { return Double.parseDouble(t); } catch (@SuppressWarnings("unused") NumberFormatException e) { /* fall through */ }
288         return s;
289      }
290   }
291
292   /**
293    * {@code #{split(s, separator)}} — splits {@code s} on the literal {@code separator}
294    * substring. Returns a JSON-array-shortcut string (e.g. {@code ["a","b","c"]}) so the
295    * result composes with other functions that accept {@code String[]}. Trailing empty fields
296    * dropped.
297    */
298   public static class Split extends TypedFunction {
299      @Override public String name() { return "split"; }
300      public String invoke(String s, String separator) {
301         if (isEmpty(s)) return "[]";
302         var parts = new ArrayList<String>();
303         if (isEmpty(separator)) {
304            parts.add(s);
305         } else {
306            var i = 0;
307            while (true) {
308               var hit = s.indexOf(separator, i);
309               if (hit < 0) { parts.add(s.substring(i)); break; }
310               parts.add(s.substring(i, hit));
311               i = hit + separator.length();
312            }
313         }
314         // Drop trailing empties.
315         while (!parts.isEmpty() && parts.get(parts.size() - 1).isEmpty())
316            parts.remove(parts.size() - 1);
317         return JsonShortcut.encodeArray(parts);
318      }
319   }
320
321   /**
322    * {@code #{join(separator, parts...)}} — concatenates {@code parts} with {@code separator}
323    * between each pair.
324    *
325    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
326    * <p>
327    * {@code #{join("/", ${tenant}, ${id})}} → {@code acme/42}
328    */
329   public static class Join extends TypedFunction {
330      @Override public String name() { return "join"; }
331      public String invoke(String separator, String[] parts) {
332         var sep = separator == null ? "" : separator;
333         var sb = new StringBuilder();
334         for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
335            if (i > 0) sb.append(sep);
336            sb.append(parts[i] == null ? "" : parts[i]);
337         }
338         return sb.toString();
339      }
340   }
341}
